questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Brazil about 8,509,361 square kilometres; France about 643,801 square kilometres; Spain about 505,990 square kilometres; Belgium about 30,688 square kilometres.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Brazil on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Brazil on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Brazil?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Brazil is the Brazilian real.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Brasília?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Brazil is Brasília.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Brazil?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Brazil article.

questions.proof: Brazil's capital city is Brasília; its most populous city is São Paulo.
